figures.title: One lane, read and written at every block
figures.caption: Every sublayer reads the residual stream, computes a correction, and adds it back. The lane holds one vector per token at width d_model from the embedding lookup to the unembedding; attention and the feed-forward network never replace it, so nothing else survives the depth.
figures.alt: A single horizontal lane labelled the residual stream: one vector per token, width d_model, never replaced. Above it, an encoder layer row with two boxes, self-attention and feed-forward, each joined to the lane by a muted arrow reading out and an accent arrow writing back. Below it, a decoder layer row with three boxes, masked self-attention, cross-attention and feed-forward, wired the same way. The encoder row is annotated two writes per layer and the decoder row three.

data.note: Attention is the only sublayer that moves information between positions; everything else is per-token. Deleting a layer at inference still leaves the lane intact.
data.lane: the residual stream: one vector per token, width d_model, never replaced

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow the lane past every sublayer.

steps.label: The lane starts as one vector per token at width d_model. It is never replaced.
Self-attention reads the lane at every position and adds its output back.
The feed-forward network reads and writes one position at a time.
An encoder layer is two sublayers, so the stream is written to twice.
Masked self-attention sees only positions up to the current one.
Cross-attention reads the encoder's final stream, the only place the two stacks meet.
A decoder layer ends with the same per-token feed-forward network.
Three sublayers, three writes. The lane is the only thing that survives the depth.

figures.title: Where the norm sits decides what the identity path carries
figures.caption: Post-norm puts LayerNorm after the addition, so the norm's Jacobian multiplies the identity term and rescaling sits directly in the gradient path. Pre-norm normalizes only the sublayer branch, leaving a bare identity term; that is why it trains without warmup, and why the stream's norm is never renormalized and grows with depth.
figures.alt: Two chains on one five-column grid: x in, norm before F, sublayer F, add, norm after add. Post-norm fills F(x), x + F(x) and LayerNorm(x + F(x)), and leaves norm before F as a dashed empty box. Pre-norm fills LayerNorm(x), F(LayerNorm(x)) and x + F(LayerNorm(x)), and leaves norm after add empty. Each chain draws an accent skip arc from x straight to the add, labelled identity.

data.note: Same five columns, same boxes. Each chain leaves exactly one column empty: that empty column is the whole argument.

chains.note: Jacobian J_N + J_N J_F. The norm's own Jacobian multiplies the identity term, so rescaling sits in the gradient path; magnitude stays bounded, and practice paid for it with learning-rate warmup.

pre-norm
GPT-2, GPT-3, LLaMA
chains.note: Jacobian I + J_F J_N. The identity term is a bare I and the norm multiplies only the branch. The stream is never renormalized, so L writes of variance v leave it with standard deviation sqrt(Lv).

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to compare where the norm sits.

steps.label: Post-norm reads x, runs the sublayer, then adds.
Only then does the norm rescale the sum, in the column after the add.
Pre-norm normalizes the input first, so the column before F is the filled one.
The add is then untouched: x arrives through a bare identity.
